_note: RACES INEC HAS DECLARED AND HAWKEYE HAS CLOSED.
A race here is finished: its result is announced, nothing more will be
reported into it, and it stops being something to follow. Adding an entry
does three things on the next boot (or on POST /api/admin/close-races):
1. every subscription it matches is deleted, so the race leaves the
follow list on the website, in Lite and in the app at once — the list
is served from one table, so there is no per-client version of this;
2. everyone who WAS following it is told who was declared, with the top
three results, in the notification centre and on their phone;
3. the Follow control stops being offered on that race anywhere.
Each of those happens ONCE — services/declarations.js records the closure in
the race_closures table, so a restart is not a second announcement.
MATCHING. `scope` is matched against subscriptions.state, which is the
region a follow was scoped to: a state for PRES/GOV/SHA and every
by-election, a senatorial district for SEN, a federal constituency for REP
(routes/subscriptions.js:reportScope). An entry with NO scope closes the
whole contest and takes every row for it — right for a by-election, which is
one seat and is over when it is over. An entry WITH a scope takes only rows
naming that region, and deliberately leaves a whole-election row alone:
somebody following all 36 governorships has not stopped following them
because one of the 36 has been declared.
WHAT THIS FILE IS NOT. It is not a result. Hawkeye does not certify
results — this records what INEC's returning officer announced, with the
sources it was taken from, so it can be checked against INEC's own sheets.
The same rule the declared card on a race page follows (app/race.js).
Numbers are transcribed by hand from the declaration; there is no endpoint
to derive them from, because IReV publishes sheet IMAGES and never figures.

_howToAdd._: Copy this into `declarations`, fill it in, restart (or POST /api/admin/close-races). Run with dryRun first — it prints the exact notification and the number of followers it would reach, and sends nothing.

declarations._announceNote: DROP THE FOLLOWS, SEND NOTHING. Osun was declared on 2026-08-16 and closed on our side a week later, both before this mechanism existed — the observers who followed it have known the result for days. Pushing it now would be a phone buzzing about last week's news, which is the fastest way to teach somebody that Hawkeye's alerts are not worth reading. Every race declared from here on carries announce:true (the default); this one entry is retrospective. The follow rows still go, which is the part that was actually wrong.
